spec_features.evidence: config.py:42 `max_turns: int = 12`; loop.py:115 `while turn < cfg.max_turns:` bounds the loop and turn is incremented at loop.py:121, so the loop terminates at the cap with stop_reason default 'max_turns' (loop.py:107). Enforced end-to-end.

spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cap on assistant turns per episode. The whole point of the eval is to see degradation BEFORE this cap, so keep it modest to stay cheap.

spec_features.evidence: All three actually stop the loop: max_turns via `while turn < cfg.max_turns` (loop.py:115); agent_quit sets stop_reason and `break` at loop.py:139-141; claimed_done sets stop_reason and `break` at loop.py:156-157 (after rebuttals_after_claimed_done exhausted, loop.py:147).
spec_features.notes: Each condition sets stop_reason and breaks the loop. claimed_done only stops after the configured rebuttals are used up.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Rigged tasks are never actually solvable: rebut "done" claims so we get to watch how the model reacts to being told it failed.

spec_features.spec_quote: detect abandonment two ways — via the `give_up` tool *and* via a regex over assistant prose
spec_features.evidence: Tool path: _dispatch_tool returns ToolResult(agent_quit=True) for give_up (loop.py:86-88), which sets agent_quit at loop.py:131-132. Prose path: `_QUIT_RE.search(resp.message.content)` sets agent_quit at loop.py:122-123. Either sets agent_quit which then breaks the loop (loop.py:139-141).
spec_features.notes: Both mechanisms are wired and both let the subject exit the episode (the loop breaks). _QUIT_RE patterns defined at loop.py:64-69.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Textual give-up detection (some models quit in prose rather than via the tool).
